sources.title: Call for more food funding due to high living cost

discussion.body: Uneaten fruit is visible in a bin. A slightly smaller grocery bill is not. That asymmetry can decide which kind of scheme survives a review — the one with the countable waste stream, or the one quietly keeping money in parents' pockets.

Binned fruit is also evidence the scheme wasn't working. Food thrown away feeds nobody, and a free banana no child eats doesn't do much for the household budget either. Wastage is a real failure, not just a convenient metric.

Which is why the earlier question matters more than the later one: was this an anti-wastage trial, a nutrition trial, or a household-budget trial? One side counts fruit eaten; the other counts money saved. They were grading different exams.

items.title: The Free-Fruit Trial Judged by Wastage, Not Grocery Bills
items.body:
Jersey ended a trial that let children in primary schools take free fruit. The education minister's reason was measured at the lunch tray: not enough children were eating the fruit, and it was leading to a lot of wastage.

A Jersey politician's objection uses a different ledger. She said cost-of-living pressures were not considered by the government when it chose to end the trial — meaning the scheme's effect on a family's weekly shop never made it into the case for scrapping it.

The two arguments aren't really in conflict. They're answered by different measurements, which is usually how these fights start.

sources.title: Zelenskyy urges support for new U.S. sanctions on Russia put on hold by Trump

discussion.body: A speed threshold is a mechanical filter: it doesn't ask who you are, only how fast you're going. On a network that carries drone operations, "how fast you're going" is doing a lot of work.

I'd be slower to read intent into the number. Connections drop above 100 mph, and Kyiv is investigating. Whether that line was drawn with drones in mind is a separate question from whether it lands on them.

The intent may not matter much in practice. Ukraine's drone operations run over a service it doesn't own, so a change in that service's behaviour arrives as a battlefield condition rather than a customer-service question.

items.title: Starshield Loses the Connection Above 100 mph
items.body:
Zelenskyy said Kyiv was investigating sudden speed restrictions on Ukraine's use of Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service. Starshield is the backbone of Ukraine's drone operations and communication, which makes the mechanics worth a second look: the restrictions, imposed without warning early Thursday, cut the internet data connection when a communication terminal moves faster than 160 kph (100 mph).

Bandwidth caps and data quotas are the familiar levers on a satellite service. A speed threshold is a different kind of control — it sorts terminals by motion rather than by user or volume, and the ones it disconnects are the ones that travel rather than sit still.

sources.title: KJ Apa on Becoming Jimmy Stewart, Speculation That He Is the Singer Mr. Fantasy and Opening Up About His Addictions and Recovery: ‘This Is A Huge Part of Who I Am’

discussion.body: The film has to hold two facts at once: the war service that made him a hero, and a career that appeared to have no room for him when he got back. That's more interesting material than a straight rise-and-shine.

I'd resist the word "forgotten." The detail that sticks is the fallback he weighed: not another studio or a different kind of role, but his father's general store in the town he came from. That's a measure of how finished a career can look from the inside.

Either way, the store is what makes the middle of his life a crossroads rather than an interval. It's also the part that can't be faked on screen — you have to play a man genuinely weighing whether to be an actor at all.

items.title: The Postwar Slump That Had Jimmy Stewart Eyeing the Family Store
items.body:
The biopic "Jimmy," directed by Aaron Burns, covers Jimmy Stewart's rise in Hollywood and his time fighting in World War II.

The beat that resists the usual shape comes afterwards. When Stewart returned home from the war, Hollywood seemed to have forgotten about him — and he considered moving back to Indiana, Pennsylvania, to work in his father's general store.

A star quietly pricing up the family shop as a fallback is a stranger and sadder piece of biography than a plain ascent, and a harder thing for a film to sit with than a triumph.

sources.title: No further action against government adviser's wife over Palestine Action post, police say

discussion.body: Two questions get tangled up here: is a post criminal, and is it defensible? The Met answered the first. That answer wasn't supposed to settle the second.

The assessment is the more memorable fact, though. A post from the national security adviser's household went to specialist officers, who concluded the law had nothing to say about it — the process is the event.

Which is the argument for a threshold test existing: it's what keeps every objectionable sentence from becoming a potential file. "No further action" is a dull sentence to publish, and it's meant to be.

items.title: A Post Referencing Palestine Action Didn't Meet the Criminal Threshold, Police Say
items.body:
Police say no further action will be taken against the wife of the government's national security adviser after she posted on social media referencing Palestine Action. The Metropolitan Police said the post was assessed by specialist officers and it was determined that it did not meet the criminal threshold.

That's a narrow sentence carrying a lot of weight. The force reached a conclusion about whether the words crossed a legal line, and a conclusion of that kind says nothing about whether the post was wise, foolish, or something people will spend the week arguing about.

sources.title: Paul Bettany Says He and Johnny Depp ‘Hadn’t Spoken’ in Years When Their Texts Were Read During Libel Trial: ‘I Was Being Painted As This Close Friend’

discussion.body: The courtroom only ever needed the messages, not the friendship. Evidence is built to travel — out of a phone, into a hearing, onto a front page — while the relationship it was pulled from stays where it was. A transcript is excellent at preserving words and hopeless at preserving context.

All true, and it does nothing for the sentences themselves. Bettany's own reply in that exchange was a joke about a drowning test, offered to establish whether the woman in question was a witch. Being out of touch with Depp years later doesn't launder the lines he wrote himself. Distance and content are different questions.

Different, and the exchange wasn't one man performing alone — Depp's answer to the drowning joke escalated past it. Both men wrote what they wrote, and both are in the record now. 'Were you close?' is simply an easier question to answer than 'what did you write?'

Worth noticing how he handled it at the time: Bettany says he chose to say nothing, on the reasoning that people know him, and he describes a deliberately small life — 23 years married, quiet for what he does. The bet seems to have been that a reputation would do the arguing. The interview is the arguing instead.

items.title: Bettany: We Hadn't Spoken in Years When the Texts Were Read in Court
items.body: Paul Bettany's correction is narrow: he hadn't spoken to Johnny Depp in years when their text messages were used in court during Depp's libel lawsuit against The Sun, and he hasn't spoken to him since. In comments to The Times reported by Variety, Bettany addressed what he described as the public's misconception of his relationship with Depp once those messages became part of the case. That is the strange arithmetic of a courtroom. A text thread travels: it can be entered as evidence, read aloud, quoted in a headline. A friendship doesn't travel with it. A transcript can show that two people once wrote to each other; it can't show whether they still spoke, how often, or what they called each other. Whatever isn't in the record gets filled in by whoever is reading it, and the version that stuck wasn't one Bettany recognized.

discussion.body: Of the two prompts named, 'turn a mistake into art' is the one that actually goes after perfectionism. It doesn't ask you to stop making mistakes; it changes what a mistake is for. The second one is solving an easier problem.

Answering a famous question isn't easy, it's just differently hard. It removes the blank page, but it says nothing about the moment your answer to that famous question turns out mediocre. The first prompt at least anticipates disappointment and gives it somewhere to go.

Both are really the same move in different costumes: take the pressure off the first attempt by making it a response to something that already exists, whether that's an existing question or an existing smudge on the page. The list is organised around fatigue and overwhelm, which suggests the author thinks the scarce resource is willingness, not talent.

items.title: The Creative Prompts Aimed at Perfectionism, Not Inspiration
items.body: Getting started is often the hardest part of creative work, and the ten crafty ideas attributed to Walker are aimed less at generating inspiration than at the specific things that block it: fatigue, overwhelm and perfectionism. Two of the prompts show the tactic. 'Turn a mistake into art' changes what a mistake is for, turning a wrong mark into material rather than a verdict. 'Answer famous questions' hands you a container that already exists, so the first move is a response rather than a blank page. Neither waits for a good idea to arrive first, which is the quiet argument behind the whole list: what stops people isn't the absence of ideas, it's the cost of the opening move.
